sanskrit: indrasya vājino vāhā hastino 'tha rathās tathā icchāmy aham ihāpūrvaṃ vāhanaṃ te surādhipa yan na viṣṇor na rudrasya nāsurāṇāṃ na rakṣasām
english: Indra has swift horses, elephants, and chariots as his conveyances. But I desire for you, O lord of the gods, a vehicle unprecedented here — one that belongs neither to Viṣṇu, nor to Rudra, nor to the asuras, nor to the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: vahantu tvāṃ mahārāja ṛṣayaḥ saṃgatā vibho sarve śibikayā rājann etad dhi mama rocate
english: Let the assembled sages carry you, O great king, O mighty lord, all together in a palanquin, O king — this is what pleases me.

sanskrit: nāsureṣu na deveṣu tulyo bhavitum arhasi sarveṣāṃ teja ādatsva svena vīryeṇa darśanāt na te pramukhataḥ sthātuṃ kaś cid icchati vīryavān
english: You should not be considered equal to the asuras or the gods — you ought to surpass them all. Draw upon the splendor of all by the mere sight of your valor. No powerful being would dare to stand before you.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca evam uktas tu nahuṣaḥ prāhṛṣyata tadā kila uvāca vacanaṃ cāpi surendras tām aninditām
english: Śalya said: Thus addressed, Nahuṣa was filled with great delight at that time. He too spoke these words to that blameless queen of the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: apūrvaṃ vāhanam idaṃ tvayoktaṃ varavarṇini dṛḍhaṃ me rucitaṃ devi tvadvaśo 'smi varānane
english: This unprecedented vehicle you have described, O fair-complexioned one, has deeply pleased me, O goddess. I am under your command, O beautiful-faced one.

sanskrit: na hy alpavīryo bhavati yo vāhān kurute munīn ahaṃ tapasvī balavān bhūtabhavyabhavatprabhuḥ
english: Indeed, one who makes sages serve as his bearers is no man of meager valor. I am an ascetic, powerful, the lord of the past, the future, and the present.

sanskrit: mayi kruddhe jagan na syān mayi sarvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam devadānavagandharvāḥ kiṃnaroragarākṣasāḥ
english: Were I to be angered, the world would cease to exist — in me all things are established. Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, serpents, and rākṣasas alike.

sanskrit: na me kruddhasya paryāptāḥ sarve lokāḥ śucismite cakṣuṣā yaṃ prapaśyāmi tasya tejo harāmy aham
english: When I am enraged, all the worlds together are not sufficient to withstand me, O bright-smiling one. Whomever I behold with my eyes, I steal away their radiance.

sanskrit: tasmāt te vacanaṃ devi kariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ saptarṣayo māṃ vakṣyanti sarve brahmarṣayas tathā paśya māhātmyam asmākam ṛddhiṃ ca varavarṇini
english: Therefore I shall carry out your word, O goddess — of this there is no doubt. The seven sages and all the brahmarṣis shall bear me. Behold our greatness and our prosperity, O fair-complexioned one.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu tāṃ devīṃ visṛjya ca varānanām vimāne yojayitvā sa ṛṣīn niyamam āsthitān
english: Having spoken thus and dismissed that lovely-faced goddess, he yoked to the celestial vehicle the sages who were devoted to their vows.

sanskrit: abrahmaṇyo balopeto matto varamadena ca kāmavṛttaḥ sa duṣṭātmā vāhayām āsa tān ṛṣīn
english: Disregarding the brāhmaṇas, drunk with power and intoxicated by the pride of the boon, acting as he willed, that wicked-souled one made those sages carry him.

sanskrit: nahuṣeṇa visṛṣṭā ca bṛhaspatim uvāca sā samayo 'lpāvaśeṣo me nahuṣeṇeha yaḥ kṛtaḥ śakraṃ mṛgaya śīghraṃ tvaṃ bhaktāyāḥ kuru me dayām
english: Dismissed by Nahuṣa, she said to Bṛhaspati: The term Nahuṣa set for me here is nearly exhausted. Seek out Śakra quickly — have mercy on me, your devoted one.

sanskrit: bāḍham ity eva bhagavān bṛhaspatir uvāca tām na bhetavyaṃ tvayā devi nahuṣād duṣṭacetasaḥ
english: The venerable Bṛhaspati said to her: Very well. You need not fear Nahuṣa, O goddess, evil-minded though he is.

sanskrit: na hy eṣa sthāsyati ciraṃ gata eṣa narādhamaḥ adharmajño maharṣīṇāṃ vāhanāc ca hataḥ śubhe
english: This vilest of men shall not endure long — he has already fallen. Ignorant of righteousness, he is as good as slain by having made the great sages serve as his bearers, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: iṣṭiṃ cāhaṃ kariṣyāmi vināśāyāsya durmateḥ śakraṃ cādhigamiṣyāmi mā bhais tvaṃ bhadram astu te
english: I shall perform a sacred rite for the destruction of this evil-minded one, and I shall find Śakra. Do not be afraid — may all be well with you.

sanskrit: tataḥ prajvālya vidhivaj juhāva paramaṃ haviḥ bṛhaspatir mahātejā devarājopalabdhaye
english: Then the immensely radiant Bṛhaspati, kindling the fire according to ritual injunction, offered the highest oblation for the purpose of recovering the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: tasmāc ca bhagavān devaḥ svayam eva hutāśanaḥ strīveṣam adbhutaṃ kṛtvā sahasāntaradhīyata
english: From that fire the venerable god Agni, the oblation-eater, himself assumed a wondrous female form and suddenly vanished.

sanskrit: sa diśaḥ pradiśaś caiva parvatāṃś ca vanāni ca pṛthivīṃ cāntarikṣaṃ ca vicīyātimanogatiḥ nimeṣāntaramātreṇa bṛhaspatim upāgamat
english: Searching through the cardinal directions and intermediate quarters, the mountains and forests, the earth and the atmosphere, moving faster than thought, he returned to Bṛhaspati in the mere twinkling of an eye.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca bṛhaspate na paśyāmi devarājam ahaṃ kva cit āpaḥ śeṣāḥ sadā cāpaḥ praveṣṭuṃ notsahāmy aham na me tatra gatir brahman kim anyat karavāṇi te
english: Agni said: O Bṛhaspati, I cannot find the king of the gods anywhere. Waters are all that remain — and I am not able to enter the waters at all. There is no path for me there, O brahmin. What else shall I do for you?

sanskrit: śalya uvāca tam abravīd devagurur apo viśa mahādyute
english: Śalya said: The preceptor of the gods said to him: Enter the waters, O greatly resplendent one.

sanskrit: agnir uvāca nāpaḥ praveṣṭuṃ śakṣyāmi kṣayo me 'tra bhaviṣyati śaraṇaṃ tvāṃ prapanno 'smi svasti te 'stu mahādyute
english: Agni said: I am not capable of entering the waters — my extinction would come about therein. I have taken refuge in you. May all be well with you, O greatly resplendent one.

sanskrit: adbhyo 'gnir brahmataḥ kṣatram aśmano loham utthitam teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati
english: Fire arose from the waters, the warrior class arose from the brahmin, iron arose from stone — their all-pervading splendor is quenched in their own original sources.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca tvam agne sarvadevānāṃ mukhaṃ tvam asi havyavāṭ tvam antaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ gūḍhaś carasi sākṣivat
english: Bṛhaspati said: You, O Agni, are the mouth of all the gods; you are the carrier of oblations. You dwell hidden within all beings and move about as their witness.

sanskrit: tvām āhur ekaṃ kavayas tvām āhus trividhaṃ punaḥ tvayā tyaktaṃ jagac cedaṃ sadyo naśyed dhutāśana
english: The wise call you one, and again they call you threefold. Were you to abandon it, this world would instantly perish, O consumer of oblations.

sanskrit: kṛtvā tubhyaṃ namo viprāḥ svakarmavijitāṃ gatim gacchanti saha patnībhiḥ sutair api ca śāśvatīm
english: The learned, having paid homage to you, attain the eternal path won by their own deeds, together with their wives and sons.

sanskrit: tvam evāgne havyavāhas tvam eva paramaṃ haviḥ yajanti satrais tvām eva yajñaiś ca paramādhvare
english: You alone, O Agni, are the carrier of oblations; you alone are the highest oblation. It is you alone that men worship with sacrificial sessions and with rites at the supreme sacrifice.

sanskrit: sṛṣṭvā lokāṃs trīn imān havyavāha; prāpte kāle pacasi punaḥ samiddhaḥ sarvasyāsya bhuvanasya prasūtis; tvam evāgne bhavasi punaḥ pratiṣṭhā
english: Having created these three worlds, O carrier of oblations, at the appointed time you cook them once more, being kindled. You are the origin of this entire universe, O Agni, and you become its resting place once again.

sanskrit: tvām agne jaladān āhur vidyutaś ca tvam eva hi dahanti sarvabhūtāni tvatto niṣkramya hāyanāḥ
english: They call you, O Agni, the giver of rain, and lightning too is nothing but you. It is from you that the seasons emerge and go forth to consume all beings.

sanskrit: tvayy āpo nihitāḥ sarvās tvayi sarvam idaṃ jagat na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cit triṣu lokeṣu pāvaka
english: All the waters are deposited in you; in you rests this entire universe. There is nothing whatsoever unknown to you in the three worlds, O purifier.

sanskrit: svayoniṃ bhajate sarvo viśasvāpo 'viśaṅkitaḥ ahaṃ tvāṃ vardhayiṣyāmi brāhmair mantraiḥ sanātanaiḥ
english: Every being seeks out its own source — enter the waters without any apprehension. I shall strengthen you with the eternal brahminical mantras.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca evaṃ stuto havyavāho bhagavān kavir uttamaḥ bṛhaspatim athovāca prītimān vākyam uttamam darśayiṣyāmi te śakraṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Śalya said: Thus praised, the venerable Agni, carrier of oblations, the supremely wise one, spoke these excellent words to Bṛhaspati with gladness: I shall show you Śakra — this I tell you truly.

sanskrit: praviśyāpas tato vahniḥ sasamudrāḥ sapalvalāḥ ājagāma saras tac ca gūḍho yatra śatakratuḥ
english: Fire then entered the waters — oceans, lakes, and ponds alike — and, concealed, came to that lake where the hundred-sacrificer lay hidden.

sanskrit: atha tatrāpi padmāni vicinvan bharatarṣabha anvapaśyat sa devendraṃ bisamadhyagataṃ sthitam
english: Then, searching through the lotus plants there, O bull of the Bhāratas, Agni perceived the lord of the gods standing concealed within the lotus stalks.

sanskrit: āgatya ca tatas tūrṇaṃ tam ācaṣṭa bṛhaspateḥ aṇumātreṇa vapuṣā padmatantvāśritaṃ prabhum
english: Coming back swiftly, he reported to Bṛhaspati that the lord was abiding within the lotus filaments, his body reduced to the size of an atom.

sanskrit: gatvā devarṣigandharvaiḥ sahito 'tha bṛhaspatiḥ purāṇaiḥ karmabhir devaṃ tuṣṭāva balasūdanam
english: Going there, accompanied by divine sages and gandharvas, Bṛhaspati then praised the god who had slain Bala with ancient hymns of praise.

sanskrit: mahāsuro hataḥ śakra namucir dāruṇas tvayā śambaraś ca balaś caiva tathobhau ghoravikramau
english: The great asura Namuci the terrible was slain by you, O Śakra, and likewise Śambara and Bala too — both of dreadful might.

sanskrit: śatakrato vivardhasva sarvāñ śatrūn niṣūdaya uttiṣṭha vajrin saṃpaśya devarṣīṃś ca samāgatān
english: Grow in strength, O performer of a hundred sacrifices; annihilate all your enemies. Rise up, O wielder of the thunderbolt, and behold the assembled divine sages who have come.

sanskrit: mahendra dānavān hatvā lokās trātās tvayā vibho apāṃ phenaṃ samāsādya viṣṇutejopabṛṃhitam tvayā vṛtro hataḥ pūrvaṃ devarāja jagatpate
english: O great Indra, the worlds were saved by you when you slew the dānavas, O mighty one. Employing the foam of waters, strengthened by the power of Viṣṇu, you formerly slew Vṛtra, O king of the gods, O lord of the universe.

sanskrit: tvaṃ sarvabhūteṣu vareṇya īḍyas; tvayā samaṃ vidyate neha bhūtam tvayā dhāryante sarvabhūtāni śakra; tvaṃ devānāṃ mahimānaṃ cakartha
english: You are the most excellent and the most praiseworthy among all beings. There exists no creature here equal to you. By you are all beings upheld, O Śakra; you have established the greatness of the gods.

sanskrit: pāhi devān salokāṃś ca mahendra balam āpnuhi evaṃ saṃstūyamānaś ca so 'vardhata śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
english: Protect the gods and those who dwell in their worlds, O great Indra; regain your strength. Thus praised in this manner, he grew in power slowly but surely.

sanskrit: svaṃ caiva vapur āsthāya babhūva sa balānvitaḥ abravīc ca guruṃ devo bṛhaspatim upasthitam
english: Resuming his own form, he became endowed with full strength. And the god addressed his teacher Bṛhaspati who stood before him.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣṭaṃ vo hatas tvāṣṭro mahāsuraḥ vṛtraś ca sumahākāyo grastuṃ lokān iyeṣa yaḥ
english: What task remains for you all? The great asura, son of Tvaṣṭṛ, has been slain — Vṛtra of the immense body, who had sought to swallow the worlds.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca mānuṣo nahuṣo rājā devarṣigaṇatejasā devarājyam anuprāptaḥ sarvān no bādhate bhṛśam
english: Bṛhaspati said: The human king Nahuṣa, by virtue of the radiance of groups of divine sages, has attained sovereignty over the gods and is tormenting us all greatly.

sanskrit: indra uvāca kathaṃ nu nahuṣo rājyaṃ devānāṃ prāpa durlabham tapasā kena vā yuktaḥ kiṃvīryo vā bṛhaspate
english: Indra said: How did Nahuṣa attain the kingship of the gods, which is so difficult to obtain? By what asceticism, or with what power? What kind of valor does he possess, O Bṛhaspati?

sanskrit: bṛhaspatir uvāca devā bhītāḥ śakram akāmayanta; tvayā tyaktaṃ mahad aindraṃ padaṃ tat tadā devāḥ pitaro 'tharṣayaś ca; gandharvasaṃghāś ca sametya sarve
english: Bṛhaspati said: The frightened gods longed for Śakra. That great position of Indra having been abandoned by you, then all the gods, the ancestors, the atharvan sages, and the assemblies of gandharvas came together.

sanskrit: gatvābruvan nahuṣaṃ śakra tatra; tvaṃ no rājā bhava bhuvanasya goptā tān abravīn nahuṣo nāsmi śakta; āpyāyadhvaṃ tapasā tejasā ca
english: And going there, O Śakra, they said to Nahuṣa: Be our king, the protector of the universe. Nahuṣa said to them: I am not capable. Nourish me with your asceticism and your splendor.

sanskrit: evam uktair vardhitaś cāpi devai; rājābhavan nahuṣo ghoravīryaḥ trailokye ca prāpya rājyaṃ tapasvinaḥ; kṛtvā vāhān yāti lokān durātmā
english: Thus addressed and strengthened by the gods, Nahuṣa of terrible might became king. And having attained sovereignty over the three worlds, that wicked-souled one made the ascetics serve as his bearers and traverses the realms.

sanskrit: tejoharaṃ dṛṣṭiviṣaṃ sughoraṃ; mā tvaṃ paśyer nahuṣaṃ vai kadā cit devāś ca sarve nahuṣaṃ bhayārtā; na paśyanto gūḍharūpāś caranti
english: He steals splendor and his gaze is poison — he is utterly dreadful. You must never behold Nahuṣa at any time. All the gods, terrified of Nahuṣa, move about in disguised forms, not revealing themselves to him.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca evaṃ vadaty aṅgirasāṃ variṣṭhe; bṛhaspatau lokapālaḥ kuberaḥ vaivasvataś caiva yamaḥ purāṇo; devaś ca somo varuṇaś cājagāma
english: Śalya said: While the foremost of the descendants of Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati, was speaking thus, the world-guardian Kubera, and ancient Yama the son of Vivasvat, the god Soma, and Varuṇa came there.

sanskrit: te vai samāgamya mahendram ūcur; diṣṭyā tvāṣṭro nihataś caiva vṛtraḥ diṣṭyā ca tvāṃ kuśalinam akṣataṃ ca; paśyāmo vai nihatāriṃ ca śakra
english: They, having come together, said to the great Indra: By good fortune Vṛtra the son of Tvaṣṭṛ has been slain. By good fortune we behold you well and unharmed, and your enemy destroyed, O Śakra.

sanskrit: sa tān yathāvat pratibhāṣya śakraḥ; saṃcodayan nahuṣasyāntareṇa rājā devānāṃ nahuṣo ghorarūpas; tatra sāhyaṃ dīyatāṃ me bhavadbhiḥ
english: Śakra addressed them all in due order and, urging them on, said: Nahuṣa of dreadful form has become king of the gods — let your assistance be given to me in this matter.

sanskrit: te cābruvan nahuṣo ghorarūpo; dṛṣṭīviṣas tasya bibhīma deva tvaṃ ced rājan nahuṣaṃ parājayes; tad vai vayaṃ bhāgam arhāma śakra
english: They replied: Nahuṣa is of dreadful form and his gaze is poisonous — we fear him, O god. But if you, O king, were to defeat Nahuṣa, then we deserve a share, O Śakra.

sanskrit: indro 'bravīd bhavatu bhavān apāṃ patir; yamaḥ kuberaś ca mahābhiṣekam saṃprāpnuvantv adya sahaiva tena; ripuṃ jayāmo nahuṣaṃ ghoradṛṣṭim
english: Indra said: So be it — let the lord Varuṇa be the lord of the waters; let Yama and Kubera this day receive the great consecration together with him. Let us conquer our enemy Nahuṣa of the terrible gaze.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraṃ jvalano 'py āha bhāgaṃ; prayaccha mahyaṃ tava sāhyaṃ kariṣye tam āha śakro bhavitāgne tavāpi; aindrāgno vai bhāga eko mahākratau
english: Then Agni too said to Śakra: Grant me a share and I shall render you assistance. Śakra said to him: There shall be your share also, O Agni — in the great sacrifice, one share shall belong jointly to Indra and Agni.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃcintya bhagavān mahendraḥ pākaśāsanaḥ kuberaṃ sarvayakṣāṇāṃ dhanānāṃ ca prabhuṃ tathā
english: Having deliberated thus, the venerable great Indra, the chastiser of Pāka, appointed Kubera as the lord of all yakṣas and lord of all wealth.

sanskrit: vaivasvataṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca varuṇaṃ cāpy apāṃ tathā ādhipatyaṃ dadau śakraḥ satkṛtya varadas tadā
english: And Śakra, the bestower of boons, duly honoring them, granted Vaivasvata lordship over the ancestors and Varuṇa lordship over the waters.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca atha saṃcintayānasya devarājasya dhīmataḥ nahuṣasya vadhopāyaṃ lokapālaiḥ sahaiva taiḥ tapasvī tatra bhagavān agastyaḥ pratyadṛśyata
english: Śalya said: Now, while the wise king of the gods was contemplating a means for the destruction of Nahuṣa together with those world-guardians, the venerable ascetic Agastya appeared there.

sanskrit: so 'bravīd arcya devendraṃ diṣṭyā vai vardhate bhavān viśvarūpavināśena vṛtrāsuravadhena ca
english: He, after honoring the lord of the gods, said: By good fortune you are prospering — through the destruction of Viśvarūpa and by the slaying of the asura Vṛtra.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā ca nahuṣo bhraṣṭo devarājyāt puraṃdara diṣṭyā hatāriṃ paśyāmi bhavantaṃ balasūdana
english: By good fortune Nahuṣa too has fallen from the kingship of the gods, O destroyer of citadels. By good fortune I see you, your enemies slain, O slayer of Bala.

sanskrit: indra uvāca svāgataṃ te maharṣe 'stu prīto 'haṃ darśanāt tava pādyam ācamanīyaṃ ca gām arghyaṃ ca pratīccha me
english: Indra said: Welcome to you, O great sage. I am gratified by the sight of you. Please accept from me water for your feet, water for rinsing the mouth, a cow, and the guest-offering.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca pūjitaṃ copaviṣṭaṃ tam āsane munisattamam paryapṛcchata deveśaḥ prahṛṣṭo brāhmaṇarṣabham
english: Śalya said: When that foremost of sages, that bull among brāhmaṇas, had been honored and was seated, the lord of the gods, filled with joy, asked him:

sanskrit: etad icchāmi bhagavan kathyamānaṃ dvijottama paribhraṣṭaḥ kathaṃ svargān nahuṣaḥ pāpaniścayaḥ
english: This I wish to hear recounted, O venerable one, O foremost of the twice-born: how Nahuṣa, of wicked resolve, fell from heaven.

sanskrit: agastya uvāca śṛṇu śakra priyaṃ vākyaṃ yathā rājā durātmavān svargād bhraṣṭo durācāro nahuṣo baladarpitaḥ
english: Agastya said: Hear, O Śakra, these glad tidings — how the wicked-souled king, the ill-conducting Nahuṣa, intoxicated with power, fell from heaven.

sanskrit: śramārtās tu vahantas taṃ nahuṣaṃ pāpakāriṇam devarṣayo mahābhāgās tathā brahmarṣayo 'malāḥ papracchuḥ saṃśayaṃ deva nahuṣaṃ jayatāṃ vara
english: The greatly fortunate divine sages and the spotless brahmarṣis, weary from carrying that evil-doing Nahuṣa, asked him a question in doubt, O god — O foremost among conquerors.

sanskrit: ya ime brahmaṇā proktā mantrā vai prokṣaṇe gavām ete pramāṇaṃ bhavata utāho neti vāsava nahuṣo neti tān āha tamasā mūḍhacetanaḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas who recite these mantras at the sprinkling of cows — are these authoritative for you or not, O Vāsava? Nahuṣa, his mind clouded by darkness, said to them: No, they are not.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ adharme saṃpravṛttas tvaṃ dharmaṃ na pratipadyase pramāṇam etad asmākaṃ pūrvaṃ proktaṃ maharṣibhiḥ
english: The sages said: You are engaged in unrighteousness; you do not accept what is righteous. This is authoritative for us — it was declared of old by the great sages.

sanskrit: agastya uvāca tato vivadamānaḥ sa munibhiḥ saha vāsava atha mām aspṛśan mūrdhni pādenādharmapīḍitaḥ
english: Agastya said: Then while he was disputing with the sages, O Vāsava, he, oppressed by unrighteousness, struck me on the head with his foot.

sanskrit: tenābhūd dhatatejāḥ sa niḥśrīkaś ca śacīpate tatas tam aham āvignam avocaṃ bhayapīḍitam
english: By that act he became bereft of splendor and stripped of fortune, O husband of Śacī. Then I spoke to him as he stood trembling and seized with fear:

sanskrit: yasmāt pūrvaiḥ kṛtaṃ brahma brahmarṣibhir anuṣṭhitam aduṣṭaṃ dūṣayasi vai yac ca mūrdhny aspṛśaḥ padā
english: Because you have corrupted what is sacred, which was established of old and practiced by the brahmarṣis — and because you have touched me on the head with your foot —

sanskrit: yac cāpi tvam ṛṣīn mūḍha brahmakalpān durāsadān vāhān kṛtvā vāhayasi tena svargād dhataprabhaḥ
english: And because you, O fool, have made sages equivalent to brahmin priests, those who are difficult to assail, serve as your bearers — by this you are cast from heaven, your splendor extinguished.

sanskrit: dhvaṃsa pāpa paribhraṣṭaḥ kṣīṇapuṇyo mahītalam daśa varṣasahasrāṇi sarparūpadharo mahān vicariṣyasi pūrṇeṣu punaḥ svargam avāpsyasi
english: Fall, O sinner, utterly fallen, your merit exhausted, to the surface of the earth. For ten thousand years you shall roam in the form of a great serpent, and when that time is fulfilled, you shall regain heaven.

sanskrit: evaṃ bhraṣṭo durātmā sa devarājyād ariṃdama diṣṭyā vardhāmahe śakra hato brāhmaṇakaṇṭakaḥ
english: Thus did that wicked-souled one fall from the kingship of the gods, O subduer of enemies. By good fortune we flourish, O Śakra — the thorn in the brāhmaṇas' side has been destroyed.

sanskrit: triviṣṭapaṃ prapadyasva pāhi lokāñ śacīpate jitendriyo jitāmitraḥ stūyamāno maharṣibhiḥ
english: Return to heaven, O husband of Śacī; protect the worlds — your senses mastered, your enemies conquered, praised by the great sages.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca tato devā bhṛśaṃ tuṣṭā maharṣigaṇasaṃvṛtāḥ pitaraś caiva yakṣāś ca bhujagā rākṣasās tathā
english: Śalya said: Then the gods were greatly delighted, surrounded by hosts of great sages, as were the ancestors, the yakṣas, the serpents, and the rākṣasas as well.

sanskrit: gandharvā devakanyāś ca sarve cāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ sarāṃsi saritaḥ śailāḥ sāgarāś ca viśāṃ pate
english: The gandharvas and the daughters of the gods, all the hosts of apsarases, the lakes, the rivers, the mountains, and the oceans, O lord of the people —

sanskrit: upagamyābruvan sarve diṣṭyā vardhasi śatruhan hataś ca nahuṣaḥ pāpo diṣṭyāgastyena dhīmatā diṣṭyā pāpasamācāraḥ kṛtaḥ sarpo mahītale
english: All came forward and said: By good fortune you flourish, O slayer of enemies. The sinful Nahuṣa has been slain — by good fortune, through the wise Agastya. By good fortune the evil-behaving one has been made a serpent on the earth.

sanskrit: śalya uvāca tataḥ śakraḥ stūyamāno gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ airāvataṃ samāruhya dvipendraṃ lakṣaṇair yutam
english: Śalya said: Then Śakra, being praised by hosts of gandharvas and apsarases, mounted Airāvata, that king among elephants, endowed with auspicious marks.

sanskrit: pāvakaś ca mahātejā maharṣiś ca bṛhaspatiḥ yamaś ca varuṇaś caiva kuberaś ca dhaneśvaraḥ
english: And Agni of great radiance, and the great sage Bṛhaspati, and Yama and Varuṇa, and Kubera the lord of wealth —

sanskrit: sarvair devaiḥ parivṛtaḥ śakro vṛtraniṣūdanaḥ gandharvair apsarobhiś ca yātas tribhuvanaṃ prabhuḥ
english: Śakra the slayer of Vṛtra, that mighty lord, surrounded by all the gods, and accompanied by gandharvas and apsarases, traversed the three worlds.

sanskrit: sa sametya mahendrāṇyā devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ mudā paramayā yuktaḥ pālayām āsa devarāṭ
english: He, the king of the gods, the performer of a hundred sacrifices, the sovereign of the gods, being reunited with Mahendrāṇī, filled with the highest joy, governed his realm.
